messages:
olivia: Heads-up — customer AcmePay (Dedicated, us-west-2) reports streaming responses arriving out-of-order after an automatic reconnect. They use Go SDK v0.8.2. Symptoms: partial JSON fragments split across events, then after a reconnect some older chunks show up after newer ones (dup + reorder). Started after our Dedicated patch last week. Ticket C-4342. Sample raw SSE below they captured.

mike_ops: Hmm. Could be client-side resume/replay logic or proxy buffering. Do they use our resume/event-id path? Which Go client exact commit? Is their iterator being used from multiple goroutines?

olivia: Go SDK v0.8.2 (released Feb). They said they never called resume explicitly, it's the SDK reconnect. Runtime name/runtime id: runtime-5c. Logs from their capture:
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] sse: conn lost, last_event_id=123456
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] sse: reconnecting...
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] sse: resuming from id=123456
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] sse: received event id=123457
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] sse: received event id=123455
```
That out-of-order line is in their client logs. They also sent raw SSE payload snippet:
```
id: 123455
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello, this is par
id: 123456
data: tial chunk"}]} 
```

alex_k: That raw snippet is interesting — `id` lines are present but it looks like events are missing the terminating `\n\n` boundary between data frames. If the proxy trims a newline during a switchover we could merge fragments or cause the client SSE parser to treat them as one event then later another event with lower id arrives. Also check whether we ever coalesce partial writes in proxy when switching backend sockets.

sara: Also can you confirm whether the customer calls `Next()` from multiple goroutines? We had a race in 0.8.1 where concurrent `Next()` + `Message()` reads could cause interleaved buffers. Example pattern that is unsafe:
```
it := client.Stream(ctx, req)
for it.Next() {
  msg := it.Message()
  go process(msg) // <- this kicks off processing concurrently while Next() continues
}
```
If the SDK's internal buffer isn't serialized, that could cause observed corruption.

devex-jay: We shipped a serialization fix in 0.8.3-rc1 that forces single-reader semantics across iterator.Next/Message and also added a small reordering-protection window on the client. Can we ask the customer to test 0.8.3-rc1? If they can't upgrade, we should try to reproduce.

olivia: I asked them to try 0.8.3-rc1 but they said they need a reproducer we can run in-house. Also they flagged duplicate billing when reconnect happens — they saw token consumption charged twice for overlapping segments.

mike_ops: Billing duplicates probably indicate our resume path retriggers token accounting. We'll need billing to confirm idempotency. @billing-bot any quick guidance? Is token accounting tied to session id or to server-side consumed token count?

billing-bot: Billing team: please attach the request IDs and timestamps. We will correlate and check whether two distinct request_ids were created for the same user session. In many cases resume creates a new billing session; that's expected but we can consider de-dup rules for short replays.

jason: Assigning to eng-runtime. Plan:
1) Pull Dedicated proxy logs for that time window and grep for event ids and `write` syscalls order.
2) Reproduce locally with Go SDK v0.8.2 against staging runtime-5c.
3) Add instrumentation to runtime to echo event IDs to logs before sending to proxy.
4) Test token-rotate/reconnect race: simulate auth refresh while stream is mid-response.

Quick repro steps for eng to try locally (suggested):
```
# start dummy generator that emits large output
./bin/serve --model dummy --response-size 1500

# grab go repro client
GODEBUG=netdns=go go run ./repro/go/sse_repro.go --sdk-version=0.8.2 --keepalive=5s

# simulate flaky network on loopback
sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 200ms loss 2%
# reproduce a drop after a few seconds to force reconnect
sleep 10; sudo tc qdisc change dev lo root netem delay 800ms loss 10%
```
This should surface event-id reordering if proxy/backends reorder buffered writes.

alex_k: Also check our SSE framing code: we expect events terminated by `\n\n`. If the runtime ever terminates with a single `\n` (e.g., `data: ...\n` but missing extra `\n`) and the proxy or client concatenates, parsers can mis-split. Add a unit test that injects partial writes from runtime and then a reorder of the write calls.

sara: Side note: if the customer's iterator code consumes messages then hands them off to goroutines that call back into SDK or call `Close()` concurrently, that was a known unsafe pattern. Recommend adding docs snippet: "Stream iterator must be read serially; do not call Next() from multiple goroutines." I'll draft.

olivia: Customer requested a hotfix. If eng-runtime reproduces quickly, what's the policy to push to Dedicated tenants? We should coordinate with ops: preflight, small canary, and rollback plan.

mike_ops: Ops: schedule a canary deploy on a single Dedicated node, monitor error rates and billing deltas, and rollback if token delta > 0.5% on customer baseline.

devex-jay: I'll message the customer with a workaround: (1) try 0.8.3-rc1, (2) ensure iterator reads are single-threaded, (3) temporarily reduce network keepalive so replays are less likely, (4) provide sample debug flags: `REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG_SSE=1` and a small script to capture raw SSE frames (we asked them to run `curl -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -s <stream-url> | hexdump -C` and send output).

support_bot: Ticket updated: escalated to eng-runtime + billing. Cc: @eng-runtime @eng-ml

olivia: I'll follow up with customer tomorrow with our repro plan and request for any additional raw captures (pcap or hexdump). For now marking thread as high-priority. :warning:
